key_insight: Small-Gradient Skipping (SGS) turns online inverse optimization updates into a mistake-driven process, yielding finite mistakes and removing the troublesome 0log T0 factor in key settings.
engineering_relevance: This can make inverse optimization more practical for sequential decision systems by reducing unnecessary updates and improving regret guarantees without expensive geometric computations.
method: Skip the learner update on rounds with no mistake when the true action is uniformly separated from alternatives.
Plug SGS into online gradient descent, online Newton step, and MetaGrad.
For M-convex action sets, achieve efficient regret bounds without computing a center of gravity.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports bounded mistakes independent of T for all three methods, and O(d^2) regret for online Newton step and MetaGrad in integer linear programming settings.
watch_item: The guarantees rely on a uniform separation condition and problem structure (e.g., M-convexity or integer linear programs), so behavior may degrade outside these assumptions.
paper_title: Online Inverse Integer Linear Optimization via Small-Gradient Skipping: Constant Regret and Finite Mistakes
